This is the common reasoning, but let's examine it objectively. I'm a programmer too. The reality in most cases is that even when something is opensource, I often don't have the time to learn a new codebase, particularly if it's a large one. Understanding a new complex codebase is a pretty significant time investment unless the software happens to be trivial. It has to be a pretty serious problem for me to spend the time it would take to debug and fix it. It's usually easier to just find other software that does what I need, or in certain cases to write my own. So, even if you or I may in some way benefit from the open part of opensource from this perspective, most everyone else really doesn't.

Everyone else is in to opensource because it's often free, as in they don't have to pay for it.
